newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases on selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases on selling pressure.

text.p: Heavy selling pressure pushed down prices of key shares at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) causing a further drop in the NSE 20-share index on Tuesday, bourse officials said.
The index lost 26.24 points to close at 3460.84. Turnover was posted at 45.373 million shillings traded on 1,355,625 shares compared to 23.308 million shillings on 385,538 points.
"There is a lot of selling pressure from speculators who are holding shares of companies which did not release spectacular results," a senior broker said.

Another broker said that the same investors were keen to buy shares in the financials. "There are actually more offers than bids at the moment, but those investors (holding financials) are sitting tight on their shares."
Foreign investors moved 624,800 shares of Firestone East Africa at between 30 and 33 from 30 and 12,500 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at 96 unchanged.
The market, fluctuating up and down in two-week cycles since January, appears to be drifting with the majority of investors watching for the financials year-end results.
"The index is not expected to move upwards until after all the companies release their results," a market analyst said.
"Definitely it's next direction will be pegged on their performance," he added.
Kenya Airways traded at a reserve price of 8.55 from 8.60 on the three-day offer board.
Bamburi Portland Cement closed at 51 from 59.50 while Kenya Power & Lighting was unchanged at 120.
Barclays Bank eased to 118 from 119 while Standard Chartered Bank gained a shilling to close at 58.

The East African Development Bank corporate bond traded 4.0 million shillings at 100.60 percent from 100.30 percent on Monday. They were offering a coupon rate of 22.75 percent applicable up to the next coupon payment date of February 22.
